items.claim: The `Context` stores unparsed/remaining arguments in `ctx.args`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Context declares `self.args` as "the leftover arguments" and `Command.parse_args` assigns the remaining unparsed tokens to `ctx.args`.

items.claim: Options with `Choice` type automatically show choices in the prompt.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_build_prompt` appends the choices when the type is a `Choice` and `show_choices` (default `True`) is set, and `Option.prompt_for_value` passes the option's type and `show_choices`.

items.claim: CliRunner's `charset` parameter defaults to "utf-8".
items.label: supported
items.reason: `CliRunner.__init__` declares `charset: str = "utf-8"`.

items.claim: `Parameter.handle_parse_result` begins by reading `ctx.params.get(name, UNSET)`, `ctx.get_parameter_source(name)`, and the explicit-default flag before any mutation.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The method opens by capturing `ctx.params.get(self.name, UNSET)`, `ctx.get_parameter_source(self.name)` and `ctx._param_default_explicit.get(...)` before any mutation.

items.claim: `Parameter.__init__` stores the raw default with `self.default = default`, keeping the `UNSET` sentinel.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `default` defaults to `UNSET` and is stored raw via `self.default = default`, with `_default_explicit` derived from it.

items.claim: `Command.main` falls back to `_detect_program_name()` when `prog_name` is not supplied, which inspects `sys.argv[0]` and the `__main__` module.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `main` calls `_detect_program_name()` when `prog_name is None`, and that helper consults `sys.modules['__main__']` and `sys.argv[0]`.

items.claim: `shell_complete` methods return `list[CompletionItem]` or `list[str]`, with strings converted to plain `CompletionItem` objects.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Parameter.shell_complete` accepts a custom completer returning `CompletionItem`s or strings and wraps plain strings in `CompletionItem(c)`.

items.claim: After the handler ladder, `Command.main` writes the recorded message and calls `sys.exit(exit_code)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: After the except ladder, `if report is not None: report()` then `sys.exit(exit_code)`.

items.claim: The `Group` class has a `commands` attribute that is a dict mapping names to `Command` objects.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Group` declares `commands: cabc.MutableMapping[str, Command]` and builds a name->Command dict from a sequence if needed.

items.claim: `CliRunner`'s `catch_exceptions` parameter defaults to `True`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The constructor signature has `catch_exceptions: bool = True`.

items.claim: `make_input_stream` encodes a `str` input with the runner's charset and wraps it in a `BytesIO`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: A `str` input is encoded with the given charset and returned wrapped in `io.BytesIO`.

items.claim: `Command.make_parser` iterates over `self.get_params(ctx)` rather than `self.params`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `make_parser` loops `for param in self.get_params(ctx)`.

items.claim: `_make_cached_stream_func` builds a closure that reads `sys.stdout` at call time, looks it up in a `WeakKeyDictionary`, and only builds a wrapper on a cache miss.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The factory's `func` calls `src_func()` (here `lambda: sys.stdout`) each call, consults a `WeakKeyDictionary` cache, and only calls `wrapper_func()` on a miss.

items.claim: `Command.get_params` runs twice during parsing and the second call to `get_help_option` returns the cached option without rebuilding it.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `parse_args` calls `get_params` via `make_parser` and again for processing, and `get_help_option` returns the cached `self._help_option` after the first construction.

items.claim: In `CliRunner.invoke`, when `capture == 'fd'` two `_FDCapture` objects are started on file descriptors 1 and 2.
items.label: supported
items.reason: When `self.capture == 'fd'`, `_FDCapture(1)` and `_FDCapture(2)` are created and started.

items.claim: `_ParsingState` has four fields: `opts` an empty dict, `largs` an empty list, `rargs` set to the caller's list, and `order` an empty list.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_ParsingState.__init__` sets `opts = {}`, `largs = []`, `rargs = rargs`, `order = []`.

items.claim: `_get_value_from_state` with `nargs == 1` checks whether the next token looks like the start of another option and returns the `FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE` sentinel if the option is allowed to stand alone.
items.label: supported
items.reason: In the `nargs == 1` branch it checks `_flag_needs_value` plus an option-like next token and yields `FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE`.

items.claim: `Option.resolve_envvar_value` returns `None` immediately when no `envvar` is declared.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: `Option.resolve_envvar_value` falls back to the `auto_envvar_prefix`-derived variable before returning `None`, so it does not return `None` immediately.

items.claim: `Context.__exit__` forwards the exception information into `ExitStack.__exit__`, so a registered resource can inspect and suppress the exception by returning true.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `__exit__` passes the exception triple to `_close_with_exception_info`, which forwards it to `ExitStack.__exit__` and returns its result.

items.claim: `BytesIOCopy.flush` flushes both its own buffer and the shared buffer.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `flush` calls `super().flush()` and then `self.copy_to.flush()`.

items.claim: `Group` sets `allow_interspersed_args` to false so remaining tokens go to a subcommand.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Group` sets `allow_interspersed_args = False` (with `allow_extra_args = True`).

items.claim: `Option.__init__` has `flag_value=Sentinel.UNSET` as the default value for the `flag_value` argument when the caller passes none.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `flag_value: t.Any = UNSET` and `UNSET` is `Sentinel.UNSET`.

items.claim: `_Option.process` appends `self.obj` — the Click-level `Option` — to `state.order` for every action.
items.label: supported
items.reason: After handling every action branch, `state.order.append(self.obj)` runs, where `obj` is the core `Option`.

items.claim: The value precedence in Click is command line, then environment variable, then `default_map`, then the parameter's default.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `consume_value` takes the parser value first, then envvar, then default map, then the parameter default.

items.claim: `BadArgumentUsage` and `BadOptionUsage` are subclasses of `UsageError`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Both `BadOptionUsage` and `BadArgumentUsage` are declared as subclasses of `UsageError`.

items.claim: `make_pass_decorator` searches up the context chain using `ctx.find_object(object_type)` or `ctx.ensure_object(object_type)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The generated decorator calls `ctx.ensure_object(object_type)` when `ensure` is set, otherwise `ctx.find_object(object_type)`, both of which walk the context chain.

items.claim: `Option._validate` checks for illegal combinations including `nargs=-1` on an option, a secondary spelling on a non-boolean flag, and `count` together with `multiple`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_validate` raises for `nargs == -1`, for secondary opts on a non-boolean flag, and for `count` with `multiple` (and with `is_flag`).

items.claim: The constant `CYGWIN` is defined as `sys.platform.startswith("cygwin")`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `CYGWIN = sys.platform.startswith("cygwin")` is defined exactly as claimed.

items.claim: In `Command.main`, an `Exit` exception supplies its own exit code.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The `except Exit as e` branch assigns `exit_code = e.exit_code`, which the teardown then passes to `sys.exit`.

items.claim: `Command.format_help()` calls format_usage, format_help_text, format_options, and format_epilog in that order.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `format_help` calls those four methods in exactly that relative order (with `format_arguments` additionally between help text and options).

items.claim: Click's source distribution includes docs/, tests/, CHANGES.rst, and uv.lock, and excludes docs/_build/.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The sdist include/exclude configuration lives in pyproject.toml, which is not shown in the provided excerpts.

items.claim: `Parameter.__init__` sets `self._default_explicit = default is not UNSET`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Parameter.__init__` literally contains `self._default_explicit = default is not UNSET`.

items.claim: The tox `docs` environment runs `sphinx-build -E -W -b dirhtml docs docs/_build/dirhtml`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: No tox configuration file is shown, so the docs environment command cannot be checked.

items.claim: Parameters marked with `required=True` raise a `MissingParameter` exception if no value is provided.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `process_value` raises `MissingParameter` when `self.required` and the value is missing.

items.claim: Click's `echo()` function is located in `click.utils` while `prompt()` and other less frequently used functions are in `click.termui`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `echo` is defined in `click/utils.py` and `prompt` (with `confirm`, `pause`, etc.) in `click/termui.py`.

items.claim: `_NamedTextIOWrapper.fileno()` returns a real descriptor only when `_original_fd` is non-negative, otherwise raising `io.UnsupportedOperation`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `fileno` returns `self._original_fd` only when it is `>= 0`, otherwise delegating to `TextIOWrapper`, which raises `io.UnsupportedOperation` for a BytesIO-backed buffer.

items.claim: The parameter source is automatically set during value resolution in `Parameter.consume_value()`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `consume_value` resolves the value and its `ParameterSource` as part of value resolution, which `handle_parse_result` then records on the context.

items.claim: `Context.invoked_subcommand` is set to the subcommand name if a single subcommand is invoked.
items.label: supported
items.reason: In non-chain mode `Group.invoke` sets `ctx.invoked_subcommand = cmd_name` for the single resolved subcommand.

items.claim: When `nargs=-1`, the argument position is marked and filled with all remaining tokens.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The `nargs` documentation states that with `nargs=-1` all remaining parameters are collected, and `Argument.add_to_parser` forwards `nargs` to the parser.

items.claim: A plain `Command` has `allow_extra_args` set to `False`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Command.allow_extra_args = False` is the class default.

items.claim: On Cygwin, `launch()` uses `cygstart`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: `launch` delegates to `_termui_impl.open_url`, and `_termui_impl.py` is not shown, so the Cygwin `cygstart` behavior cannot be checked.

items.claim: `ClickException` has attributes `message` and `exit_code` and methods `show()` and `format_message()`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `ClickException` defines `exit_code`, `message`, `format_message()`, and `show()`.

items.claim: `strip_ansi` applies a CSI regular expression to the output string.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `strip_ansi` calls `_ansi_re.sub("", value)` where `_ansi_re` is the CSI escape-sequence regex.

items.claim: `BytesIOCopy.write` returns the number of bytes written.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `BytesIOCopy.write` returns `super().write(b)`, i.e. the byte count written.

items.claim: `click.make_pass_decorator()` accepts an `ensure` parameter that creates the object if not found.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `make_pass_decorator(object_type, ensure=False)` calls `ctx.ensure_object` (creating and storing the object) when `ensure` is true.

items.claim: CliRunner's isolation sets `formatting.FORCED_WIDTH` to a fixed value of 80.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `isolation` sets `formatting.FORCED_WIDTH = 80` and restores the old value afterwards.

items.claim: Because of `value_proc`, a prompted answer that fails conversion is rejected and the prompt is repeated rather than crashing.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The `value_proc` is passed to `termui.prompt`, but termui.py is not shown, so the retry-on-failure behavior cannot be confirmed from the given code.

items.claim: The `Parameter.expose_value` attribute defaults to `True`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Parameter.__init__` declares `expose_value: bool = True` and stores it unchanged.

items.claim: `_main_shell_completion` returns immediately when the completion environment variable is unset.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_main_shell_completion` reads the env var and returns early when `not instruction`.

items.claim: The `options_metavar` default is `"[OPTIONS]"`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Command.__init__` has `options_metavar: str | None = "[OPTIONS]"`.

items.claim: Click produces an error like "Error: Invalid value for '--count': 'abc' is not a valid integer" for an invalid type.
items.label: supported
items.reason: IntParamType's name is "integer" and the failure message is formatted as "Invalid value for <hint>: {value!r} is not a valid integer." prefixed with "Error: ".

items.claim: `click.make_pass_decorator()` creates custom decorators to pass specific object types.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `make_pass_decorator(object_type, ensure)` returns a decorator that finds/creates an object of the given type and passes it as the first argument.

items.claim: `Context._default_map_has` returns `False` when the context has no default map.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_default_map_has` requires `self.default_map is not None`, so a missing map yields `False`.

items.claim: The `_Option.action` field supports the values store_const, append, append_const, and count.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_Option.process` handles "store", "store_const", "append", "append_const" and "count" actions.

items.claim: When `default=True` is set with a `flag_value`, the parameter receives the `flag_value`, not the boolean `True`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_resolve_lazy_default` substitutes `True` with the flag activation value for flag options, and `get_default` applies it.

items.claim: `click.Path` validates file/directory paths.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The `Path` type performs existence, file/dir, readable/writable/executable checks on path values.

items.claim: The `Context.default_map` is accessed via `Context.lookup_default(name, call=True)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Context.lookup_default(self, name, call=True)` reads the value from `default_map`.

items.claim: `_safe_write` calls `ansi_wrapper.reset_all()` and re-raises when an exception occurs.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: No `_safe_write` appears in any shown file (utils.py is not included), so the claim cannot be checked.

items.claim: If the two entered values do not match in a confirmation prompt, Click echoes "Error: The two entered values do not match.".
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The confirmation-prompt message lives in `termui.py`, which is not shown.

items.claim: `Option.process_value` has a shortcut for unset boolean flags and otherwise falls through to `Parameter.process_value`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The override returns early (value `False`, optional callback) for unset boolean flags and otherwise calls `super().process_value`.

items.claim: The context stack used by `get_current_context()` is thread-local.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The stack lives on `_local = local()` from `threading`, so it is thread-local.

items.claim: The second pass of `_OptionParser.parse_args` calls `_unpack_args` to distribute remaining tokens to declared positional arguments.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_process_args_for_args`, the second pass, calls `_unpack_args` with the declared arguments' nargs.

items.claim: `_OptionParser.parse_args` wraps the argument list in a `_ParsingState` and runs two passes: options first, then positional arguments.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `parse_args` builds `_ParsingState(args)` then runs `_process_args_for_options` followed by `_process_args_for_args`.

items.claim: The Windows error codes used include ERROR_SUCCESS = 0 and ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY = 8.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `ERROR_SUCCESS = 0` and `ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY = 8` are defined exactly as claimed.

items.claim: In `handle_parse_result`, writing the value into `ctx.params` is conditional on `expose_value`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The winning branch writes `ctx.params[self.name]` only `if self.expose_value`.

items.claim: A `default_map` can be passed at invocation as `cli(default_map={'runserver': {'port': 5000}})`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Calling the command forwards extra kwargs through `main`/`make_context` to the `Context` constructor's `default_map`, which is looked up per subcommand `info_name`.

items.claim: `MissingParameter` extends `BadParameter` and has a `param_type` attribute of 'option', 'argument', or 'parameter'.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `MissingParameter(BadParameter)` stores `param_type` documented as 'parameter', 'option' or 'argument'.

items.claim: The `should_strip_ansi` replacement installed by `CliRunner.isolation` ignores the stream and answers from the `color` argument, returning `True` when `color=False`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The replacement `should_strip_ansi` ignores `stream`, returning `not default_color` when `color is None` and `not color` otherwise, i.e. `True` for `color=False`.

items.claim: Returning a value from a Click command callback has no effect on the process exit code; success exits with code 0.
items.label: supported
items.reason: In standalone mode the return value `rv` is deliberately not used; `ctx.exit()` is called with the default code 0.

items.claim: For an option declared with `default=1`, `_guess_type` sees an `int` and `convert_type` returns the `INT` singleton.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_guess_type(None, 1)` returns `type(1)` i.e. `int`, and `convert_type` returns the `INT` singleton for `int`.

items.claim: `CommandCollection` is a subclass in the command hierarchy along with `Group` under `Command`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Group` subclasses `Command` and `CommandCollection` subclasses `Group`, so both sit in the command hierarchy under `Command`.

items.claim: For Fish completion, `COMP_CWORD` contains the partial word being completed rather than an index.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The fish completion script and its use of `COMP_CWORD` live in `shell_completion.py`, which is not shown.

items.claim: In `prompt()`, if `value_proc` is None, it is set to `convert_type(type, default)`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The body of `prompt()` is in `termui.py`, which is not shown.

items.claim: The `CliRunner.isolation` generator yields the three buffers.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The generator yields the tuple `(stream_mixer.stdout, stream_mixer.stderr, stream_mixer.output)`.

items.claim: `click.STRING` converts to Python `str` and is the default type.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `StringParamType.convert` returns `str` and STRING is documented/used as the implicit default type.

items.claim: `Command.make_parser` constructs an `_OptionParser` and then asks every parameter to register itself with it.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `make_parser` creates `_OptionParser(ctx)` and calls `param.add_to_parser(parser, ctx)` for each param.

items.claim: The `Abort` exception is a subclass of `ClickException` and exits with status code 1.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: `Abort` subclasses `RuntimeError`, not `ClickException`, and carries no exit code.

items.claim: `_find_binary_reader()` tests `stream.read(0)` to determine if the stream is binary and falls back to `stream.buffer`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_is_binary_reader` uses `stream.read(0)` and `_find_binary_reader` falls back to the stream's `buffer` attribute.

items.claim: The Click test matrix includes a free-threaded Python 3.14t configuration on ubuntu-latest.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The workflow file's contents are not shown, so the matrix entries cannot be checked.

items.claim: When no `prog_name` is given in `extra`, `CliRunner.invoke` falls back to `get_default_prog_name`, which returns the command's own name.
items.label: supported
items.reason: On `KeyError` from `extra.pop("prog_name")` it calls `get_default_prog_name`, which returns `cli.name or "root"`.
